name: Marlin Stutzman

on_the_ballot: Running, Republican for U.S. House (IN) - District 3

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "For years we marched in Right To Life marches in Washington, Fort Wayne and across the nation, demanding that our leaders reverse the disastrous decision made by the Supreme Court in 1973 legalizing abortion. I authored multiple bills on the state and federal level trying to protect the lives of the unborn in any way possible. Now that Roe vs. Wade has been overturned, our battle to protect life is not over. We must continue to ensure that every life, born and unborn, is valued and protected. There is still work to do on both the state and federal level and I will never stop working to create a culture that values every life in America."

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "We can preserve Social Security and Medicare for the next generation and still enact thoughtful reforms to our nation's entitlement structure to reduce our national debt and the threat it poses to our children and grandchildren. It's time for Washington to get out of the way and allow American workers to get back to work!"

positions.question: Do you support increasing security along the southern US border?

evidence.text: "Our broken border with Mexico is beyond a crisis, and doublespeak and finger pointing are all we see from the politicians in Washington. The far left and open border globalists have zero respect for our national sovereignty, and they are currently aiding an invasion into our country. We know there are drugs flowing into every state in our nation and criminal cartels are getting a foothold here is the United States. In addition, the staggering number of illegals are no doubt allowing terrorist or spy networks to infiltrate the homeland. We need to finish the wall, fund the necessary law enforcement personnel and provide the technical resources to close our border once and for all. Until our border is fixed there should be no discussion of immigration changes or reforms."
